title: Identify the quadrants
text: Cosine represents the $$x-$$ coordinate on the unit circle. Since the value is positive, the angles must be located in the first and fourth quadrants.

title: Find the specific angles
text: The angle in the first quadrant where cosine equals $$\frac{1}{2}$$ is $$\frac{\pi}{3}.$$ The corresponding angle in the fourth quadrant is $$\frac{-\pi}{3}$$ (which is equivalent to $$\frac{5\pi}{3}$$ ).

title: Add periodicity
text: The cosine function has a period of $$2\pi.$$ To capture all possible coterminal solutions, add integer multiples of the period ( $$2n\pi$$ ) to both angles.

title: Final Expression
text: The general solutions can be written compactly as $$\theta=\pm\frac{\pi}{3}+2n\pi.$$
